content: Indinavir affects the metabolism of drugs processed by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction can lead to increased levels or effects of certain drugs, necessitating careful monitoring and potential dose adjustments. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs: 1. Felodipine: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust the dose of felodipine as needed. Felodipine also increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter inhibition. 2. Fesoterodine: Indinavir raises the levels or effects of fesoterodine through CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor and adjust therapy as necessary. 3. Fluconazole: Fluconazole increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 4. Fludrocortisone: Indinavir increases fludrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter inhibition. Monitor for toxicity and adjust therapy as required. 5. Flunisolide (inhaled): Indinavir increases flunisolide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 6. Flurazepam: Indinavir increases flurazepam levels through CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Consider alternative benzodiazepines or reduce the dose of flurazepam. Monitor closely. 7. Fluticasone (furoate and inhaled): Indinavir increases fluticasone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may significantly increase systemic exposure to fluticasone, necessitating caution and monitoring. 8. Fluvastatin: Indinavir increases fluvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, increasing the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Fluvoxamine: Fluvoxamine increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 10. Fosamprenavir: Indinavir and fosamprenavir mutually increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, raising the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 11. Fosaprepitant: Fosaprepitant increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and indinavir increases fosaprepitant levels similarly. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 12. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 13. Fostamatinib: Indinavir increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and fostamatinib increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor for toxicities and consider dose adjustments. 14. Garlic: Garlic decreases indinavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Gefitinib: Indinavir increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 16. Gentamicin: Indinavir increases gentamicin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 17. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Indinavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely. 18. Glimepiride, Glipizide, Glyburide: Indinavir decreases the effects of these drugs, likely due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor for hyperglycemia and adjust therapy as needed. 19. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases indinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 21. Guanfacine: Indinavir increases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. For extended-release guanfacine, reduce the dose by half when coadministered. Monitor for adverse effects. 22. Hydrocodone: Indinavir increases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 23. Hydrocortisone: Indinavir increases hydrocortisone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 24. Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Indinavir increases hydroxyprogesterone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 25. Ifosfamide: Indinavir decreases ifosfamide levels by inhibiting its metabolism to active alkylating metabolites, potentially reducing efficacy. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 26. Iloperidone: Indinavir increases iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and iloperidone increases indinavir levels similarly. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 27. Imatinib: Indinavir increases imatinib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 28. Imipramine: Indinavir increases imipramine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 29. Insulin (various types): Indinavir decreases the effects of insulin due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor for hyperglycemia and adjust therapy as needed. 30. Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 31. Istradefylline: Indinavir increases istradefylline levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and istradefylline increases indinavir levels similarly. Monitor closely and consider dose adjustments. 32. Itraconazole: Itraconazole increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the indinavir dose to 600 mg every 8 hours when coadministered. 33. Ivacaftor: Indinavir increases ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when coadministered. Ivacaftor also increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. 34. Ivermectin: Indinavir increases ivermectin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 35. Ixabepilone: Indinavir increases ixabepilone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 36. Ketamine: Indinavir decreases ketamine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 37. Ketoconazole: Ketoconazole increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 38. Lacosamide: Indinavir increases lacosamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Consider reducing the lacosamide dose when coadministered. 39. Lamivudine: Indinavir and lamivudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 40. Lapatinib: Indinavir increases lapatinib levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 41. Lenacapavir: Lenacapavir increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 42. Letermovir: Indinavir increases letermovir levels by decreasing its metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 43. Levamlodipine: Indinavir increases levamlodipine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema, and adjust the dose as necessary. 44. Levoketoconazole: Levoketoconazole increases indinavir levels via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 45. Levomilnacipran: Indinavir increases levomilnacipran levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Do not exceed 80 mg/day of levomilnacipran when coadministered. 46. Linagliptin: Indinavir decreases linagliptin effects but also increases its levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 47. Liraglutide: Indinavir decreases liraglutide effects due to insulin resistance caused by protease inhibitors. Monitor for hyperglycemia and adjust therapy as needed. 48. Lomitapide: Lomitapide increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Consider reducing the dose of lomitapide when coadministered. 49. Loperamide: Indinavir increases loperamide levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. 50. Lopinavir: Indinavir and lopinavir mutually increase each other's levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely. 51. Loratadine: Indinavir increases loratadine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and loratadine increases indinavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely. 52. Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Indinavir increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as necessary. This list provides detailed drug interactions with indinavir, emphasizing the need for careful monitoring, dose adjustments, and consideration of alternative therapies where appropriate.
